A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain complete main text and Appendices A–D. Their text, equations, tables, figure, and proofs support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original deferral experiments on four image datasets in Tables 2–3 and a synthetic Mixture-of-Gaussians experiment in Figure 1.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, including system accuracies, deferral ratios, and the synthetic experiment’s learning curves.

M1.justification: The single-stage and two-stage surrogate loss families, auxiliary functions, and prediction/deferral procedures in Sections 3–4 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN, Tiny ImageNet, and the realizable Mixture-of-Gaussians scenario. The additional application areas discussed in related work are not newly evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains Verma et al. (2023) and Mao et al. (2024a); Table 3 retains Mao et al. (2023a). Figure 1 also retains the same comparators. Newly cited works are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 6 retains ResNet-16, 200 training epochs, Adam, batch size 1024, and the same classification-error costs and expert-domain assignments. Metrics and the synthetic experiment’s sample-size sweep are unchanged.

E4.justification: The realizability and training-sample-size analysis in Figure 1 is unchanged. References to adversarial robustness and top-k deferral describe other research, rather than new analyses performed by this work.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over five runs, omit standard deviations for deferral ratios, and show the same error bars in Figure 1. No uncertainty-reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 2–3 and the curves in Figure 1 are unchanged. For example, the proposed method’s CIFAR-10 accuracy remains 92.21 ± 0.18% for single-stage and 93.34 ± 0.18% for two-stage deferral.

T1.justification: Definitions, assumptions, theorems, and derivations in Sections 2–5 and Appendices B–D are unchanged. References to Enhanced H-consistency bounds change from Mao et al. (2024e) to Mao et al. (2025b), identifying the same cited work rather than a mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: realizable consistency, consistency bounds, Bayes-consistency, and enhanced low-noise guarantees for multiple-expert deferral.

C2.justification: The interpretations of comparable non-realizable accuracy, improved realizable performance, and different deferral behavior remain unchanged. Section 7 retains the same qualifications and future directions concerning overlapping expertise, heterogeneous data, unavailable expert predictions, and LLM applications.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain identical, including the architecture, optimizer, weight decay, batch size, and expert construction. v2 adds no implementation instructions, hardware details, or code/data access information.

R1.justification: v2 adds seven references covering balanced classification, budgeted deferral, noise-dependent consistency bounds, adversarial robustness, query allocation, and top-k deferral. Sections 2 and 5 and Appendix A gain corresponding citations or brief descriptions, without substantially revising the paper’s novelty positioning.

P1.justification: Appendix A briefly expands its survey and application list, while citation labels and bibliography information are updated. The main narrative, terminology, and section organization remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Additional references reflow the bibliography on pages 11–14, and Appendix A’s expansion shifts text on pages 16–17. Tables 1–3 and Figure 1 retain their design, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 provides a more complete literature context by acknowledging budgeted, robust, query-allocation, and top-k deferral research absent from v1’s survey, alongside additional consistency literature. This is a limited scholarly improvement; the methods, theoretical development, empirical evidence, and stated limitations remain unchanged.
